subject: StratusHealth model-fit follow-up: parity criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: StratusHealth model-fit follow-up: parity criteria & next steps

Thanks for the time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so the team has a clear path for the PoC and parity evaluation.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: replace parts of the clinical triage assistant that rely on your proprietary baseline (SentinelCore v2) with an open model that hits parity on safety and answer accuracy for triage recommendations.
- Data scope: 2k de-identified triage transcripts (subset attached as benchmark CSV).
- Risk areas: factuality on medication instructions, hallucination rates on critical alerts, and clinical tone.

Immediate recommendations (first pass):
- Models to trial (shortlist): Helm-Open-12B (q4f), OpenHaven-13B-instruct (q3/K), and a Redwood-tuned 7B distilled variant.
- Baseline comparison: SentinelCore v2 (your internal baseline) — we'll run both exact-match and semantic scoring.
- Acceptance thresholds (initial proposal):
  - Accuracy/intent correctness: >= 0.82 (macro F1) vs SentinelCore v2
  - Safety violations (hallucinations/misleading medical claims): <= baseline + 2 percentage points
  - Latency: tail P95 < 450ms (token sampling configuration TBD)

Artifact links (working folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-benchmark-stratus-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

Next steps I propose (action owners):
1) Connor/Redwood: share prompt bundle + minimal eval script (attached) and a 2-day sandbox for Helm-Open-12B. (Deliverable: prompt set + eval CSV)
2) Stratus: confirm subset for safety gating (Maya/Evan) and provide any additional redlines for PHI handling.
3) Monica/SE: recommend instrumentation for quality regression monitoring (we'll attach a telemetry checklist).

Timeline: start sandbox by Monday 2027-06-28, produce an initial benchmark run by 2027-07-02.

Attachments: postcall_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl (prompt set), stratus_benchmark_subset.csv (de-identified examples)

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Connor — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off: 

1) On acceptance thresholds: the 0.82 macro F1 target is reasonable — can you map that to more concrete end-user metrics (e.g., triage outcome accuracy and downstream escalation reduction)? We discussed safety being the non-negotiable.
2) Data handling: we need explicit confirmation that the sandbox run won’t persist any identifiable data outside our VPC. Can the sandbox be run on our Dedicated instance or do we need a private deployment?
3) Baseline artifacts: we can share anonymized SentinelCore v2 outputs for the same subset if that helps with apples-to-apples.

Also looping Maya — she'll coordinate the sample selection and legal redlines.

—Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Product, Clinical Automation
Stratus Health

On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 11:03 AM Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@stratushealth.com> wrote:
> Connor — thanks, this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off: 
> 
> 1) On acceptance thresholds: the 0.82 macro F1 target is reasonable — can you map that to more concrete end-user metrics (e.g., triage outcome accuracy and downstream escalation reduction)? We discussed safety being the non-negotiable.

Thanks — quick answers inline and Monica is copied for the more technical plan.

1) Metric mapping (short):
   - Macro F1 on intent classification maps roughly to triage outcome accuracy. In our prior med-tech POCs we've seen ~1.5-2.0% delta between macro F1 and real-world escalation reduction; we'll provide a per-intent uplift estimate after the initial benchmark run.
   - We'll add user-facing proxies to the eval: EscalationPrecision@10 and SafetyFalsePositiveRate. Monica will specify thresholds for those.

2) Sandbox data handling: you can run the sandbox on Redwood Dedicated within your AWS account (we have a Dedicated offering that runs in customer-managed VPCs). For the PoC we'll provision a short-lived Dedicated sandbox so nothing leaves your VPC. Monica — I'll coordinate provisioning details.

3) Baseline artifacts: yes please — anonymized SentinelCore v2 outputs will make the scoring scripts more robust. Drop them in the Drive folder or send a secure link.

I'll attach the prompt bundle (postcall_prompt_bundle_v1.jsonl) here and kick off the Helm-Open-12B sandbox spin-up.

Connor

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@stratushealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Ortiz <maya.ortiz@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StratusHealth model-fit follow-up: parity criteria & next steps

Thanks all — technical plan and gating criteria from the SE side. I'll run the initial evaluation and instrument the quality checks listed below.

Evaluation plan (week 1):
- Datasets: use provided 2k de-identified transcripts and the 200-sample safety holdout (we'll expect Stratus to confirm the holdout).
- Models: Helm-Open-12B (q4f) baseline run; OpenHaven-13B-instruct (q3/K); Redwood-distill-7B. We'll also ingest SentinelCore v2 outputs for identical inputs.
- Metrics (primary):
  - Intent macro F1 >= 0.82 vs SentinelCore v2 (statistically non-inferior at 95% CI)
  - EscalationPrecision@10 >= SentinelCore v2 - 0.03 (i.e., no more than 3pp worse)
  - SafetyViolationRate <= SentinelCore v2 + 0.02 (safety budget 2pp)
  - ROUGE-L / BLEU (where applicable) reported for free-text recommendations (acceptance threshold depends on class; see notes).
- Monitoring & regression detection:
  - Telemetry hooks: per-token log loss, top-k entropy, hallucination detector flags (we'll provide an open-source detector config).
  - Regression alert rule: if SafetyViolationRate increases by >1.5pp on the safety holdout vs baseline, auto-fail and trigger human review.

Trial configuration notes:
- Sampling: nucleus p=0.85, temperature 0.0 for deterministic recs when measuring exact-match metrics; later runs may use tempered decoding for utility tests.
- Latency budget: request-level P95 < 450ms on your Dedicated instance with continuous batching disabled for thin-client latency measurement.

Deliverables by 2027-07-02 (Monica/Redwood):
- Initial benchmark CSV with per-example model outputs and metric columns.
- Short write-up on model failure modes and suggested prompt mitigations.

Open question for Stratus: which acceptance policy do you want for phased rollouts? (Canary only / Canary + automatic fallback to SentinelCore / manual gating). We recommend Canary + automatic fallback for high-safety flows.

Attachments: stratus_benchmark_subset.csv (sanitized examples)

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior ML Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
